X.note: The stone wall texture is decent, but the parapet is missing. Without it the bastion reads as a low flat slab, and the terreplein is a sunken grey-rubble bowl. The background buildings are untextured grey boxes. The frames are stable, with no flicker.

Y.note: The wall is smooth, near-white and plasticky, with a faint fine texture and no individual stones. The deck is flat dark asphalt-like grey, which looks anachronistic and modern. There is no parapet. It looks like an unfinished mockup. The frames are stable.

Z.note: Best of the three. The ashlar wall has weathering, waterline algae and stains. It has a proper parapet and a believable earthen/gravel terreplein, and the lighting is plausible. Small cannon models are the only weak point. The backdrop buildings are still plain grey blocks. The texture stays fixed to the wall across frames.

why: Z has a convincingly weathered masonry wall, a complete parapet and an earthen deck, while Y is a smooth white plastic form with an asphalt-like deck and X has no parapet and a sunken rubble surface.
anachronisms_seen: plain untextured grey modern-looking block buildings in background (all)
missing parapet leaving the bastion looking like a modern quay slab (X, Y)
